searched: Searched 2026-10-15 for 2019–2026 founding, founder, leadership and departure records of DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Zhipu, MiniMax, Baichuan, 01.AI, StepFun and Alibaba's Qwen team. Primary sources retrieved and used: the HKEX prospectuses of Zhipu (English 2025123000017 and Chinese 2025123000018_c, 30 Dec 2025) and MiniMax (English 2025123100025, 31 Dec 2025), located through the HKEXnews title-search API; company pages of Moonshot AI (moonshot.cn/about), Baichuan (baichuan-ai.com, through the reader relay because the site is a script-rendered shell), 01.AI (lingyiwanwu.com/about.html); Yang Zhilin's personal site (kimiyoung.github.io; commented-out HTML sections were not used); Junyang Lin's X post of 3 March 2026 (via X syndication). Reporting used only where no primary text could be retrieved: SCMP 2024-08-07 (paywalled; only the opening paragraph is available), 科创板日报 2024-03-23 via Eastmoney, 量子位 via 36Kr 2026-01-27, Caixin Global 2026-03-04. Not retrievable or not usable: Moonshot and StepFun official WeChat articles (empty shells), stepfun.com company pages (script-rendered; relay returned navigation only), DeepSeek pages (homepage, careers, transparency centre give no founding date or founder statement), and no Reddit AMA or Moonshot page naming its co-founders was found. DeepSeek's founding date (reported variously as May or July 2023 from business-registration databases) was dropped: no primary or reputable dated report was retrieved. HKEX post-listing filings of Zhipu (Z.AI) and MiniMax through October 2026 were listed; they show only independent non-executive director changes and a 2026 Zhipu English-name change, which were left out. Zhipu director resignations visible only in remuneration tables were left out. Baichuan and 01.AI co-founder departures and Alibaba's reported internal messages after Lin's post were found only in secondary reporting and left out. Quote-limit note: the checker counts whitespace-separated words, so a Chinese quote counts as one word and Chinese pages report a document length of about 0; Chinese quotes were kept to at most about 45 characters each and a few per source.
